title: Schultz Out With Groin Injury; KWIII Misses Thanksgiving Showdown – NBC Sports Report
body:
Ken Walker III will miss the Buffalo Bills matchup on Thanksgiving, a blow to the New York Jets’ offensive plans as the team heads into the season’s most high‑profile weekend. The veteran running back was diagnosed with a groin strain during the week’s practice sessions, and according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the injury is severe enough to keep him sidelined for the Thursday night contest. The loss forces head coach Robert Saleh and his staff to re‑evaluate their ground game against a Bills defense that has shown a knack for containing the run.

Walker, who joined the Jets in 2022 after a productive stint with the Seattle Seahawks, has been a versatile weapon out of the backfield. He contributed 437 rushing yards and three touchdowns in 2023, while also adding 241 receiving yards. His blend of power and pass‑catching ability has been especially valuable in a offense that has struggled to establish a consistent aerial rhythm. With the Jets sitting at 5‑5 heading into Week 12, the timing of his injury could prove pivotal, as the team looks to secure a win that would keep its playoff hopes alive.

The Bills, meanwhile, have built a reputation this season for a stout defensive front that excels at forcing turnovers and limiting yards after contact. Defensive coordinator Leslie Frazier’s unit has allowed just 3.9 yards per carry, ranking among the league’s best. Without Walker’s ability to pick up blitzes and serve as a safety valve for quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the Jets may find themselves forced into a one‑dimensional passing attack, a scenario that the Bills are well‑equipped to exploit. Analysts point out that Buffalo’s secondary, anchored by Tre'Davious White and Jordan Poyer, could tighten coverage on the Jets’ receivers, making the absence of a reliable third‑down back even more consequential.

Coach Saleh has already hinted at a potential reshuffle of the running back rotation. Veteran Breece Hall, who has been sharing carries with Walker, is expected to shoulder a larger workload. Hall’s recent performances have shown flashes of explosiveness, but he has also been plagued by injuries of his own, raising concerns about durability. The Jets could also turn to rookie running back Michael Carter, who has displayed promise in limited snaps. However, relying heavily on a less experienced backfield against a disciplined Bills defense is a gamble that could backfire if the offense stalls early.

Beyond the immediate tactical implications, Walker’s injury underscores a broader issue for the Jets: depth at skill positions. The team has been hit hard by injuries this season, with key contributors on both sides of the ball missing significant time. The front office has already been active in the trade market, seeking to bolster the roster before the trade deadline. If the Jets can acquire a proven veteran or a high‑upside prospect to fill the void, it could mitigate the impact of Walker’s absence and provide a boost for the final stretch of the season.

Looking ahead, the Thanksgiving game will serve as a litmus test for the Jets’ adaptability. A strong showing from the remaining backs, combined with effective game‑planning from the coaching staff, could keep New York competitive despite the setback. Conversely, a lackluster performance may widen the gap between the Jets and the AFC East’s top contenders, making a postseason berth increasingly elusive. As the league’s spotlight turns to Thursday night, the Jets must find a way to compensate for the loss of Ken Walker III and prove that they can thrive even when key pieces are missing.
